news.2026-11-20-pologne-missiles-russes-: Poland: two Russian missiles and a drone crash on its soil during a massive attack on Ukraine, Tusk denounces an "intentional provocation"

Overnight from Thursday 19 to Friday 20 November, two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone entered Polish airspace and crashed in the south-east of the country. One was a Kh-101 cruise missile that came down in Nowy Lipowiec, 60 km from Ukraine. Nobody was injured [1][3].

According to Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, three Russian objects, probably two missiles and a jet-powered drone, violated Polish airspace during a large-scale Russian attack on Ukraine [1][3][6].

"In Nowy Lipowiec, we can already confirm it was a Kh-101 missile," the minister said [2]. The missile fell in a field at the edge of a forest in Lublin province, about 60 km from the Ukrainian border, and caught fire a few hundred metres from the village's first houses [1][2].
A second projectile, probably a cruise missile, fell near Rudnik nad Sanem, and a suspected drone crashed in Mołodycz [1][4]. There were no injuries and no damage to critical infrastructure [1][3].

The first warning signals reached Polish command at 1:40 am; Polish F-16s and Swedish Gripens patrolled all night, and Swedish pilots tried to intercept the object believed to be the Kh-101, but bad weather prevented visual identification [7].

That night, Russia fired 26 Kalibr missiles, 72 Kh-101 missiles and 503 drones at Ukraine, according to the Polish military [1]. Ukraine's Prime Minister reported eight people killed, six of them in Kyiv [8].

Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it an "intentional provocation" and convened his ministers, army representatives and the heads of the security services [3][4]. He linked the incident to the military exercises of the "coalition of the willing", Kyiv's allies, which were taking place in Poland at the same time [1][4].

Kosiniak-Kamysz denounced "another provocation by the Russian Federation" and said he would ask NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte for more forces for Operation Eastern Sentry, as well as an additional AWACS radar aircraft [5]. Moscow did not immediately comment, according to AP [3].
Key takeaway: Russian cruise missiles fell on the territory of a NATO country, protected by the Alliance's collective defence, which raises tension between Moscow and Europe a notch further [1][3].

Mark Rutte said NATO "stands in solidarity with Poland" and called the incident "clearly dangerous, a consequence of Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine" [3]. The United Kingdom and Ukraine also condemned the incident [2].

It is not the first time: a Kh-101 had already crashed on 30 July in Tarnawa-Kolonia, in eastern Poland [1]. In November 2022, in Przewodów, a Ukrainian air-defence missile killed two Poles [10]. Eastern Sentry, NATO's air-defence mission on its eastern flank, was launched after the Russian drone incursions of September 2025 [9].

For you, this shows that the war in Ukraine can spill over into the European Union's neighbours. France takes part in air defence on NATO's eastern flank: if the Alliance reinforces Eastern Sentry, it could be asked to send more aircraft or troops.
